summary: Siu-tong Kwan works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti, and also studied under Zhihua Yao in 2005.

So Takahashi is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo and held posts at Meijo University, where he is attested as associate professor (1977–1978) and professor (1991).

Sodo Mori specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1968) and served as professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1993–1997), lecturer at Toyo and Taisho universities, and Pali Text Society representative in Japan (attested 1985).
Sodo Yokoyama was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Eiko Hashimoto and Kodo Sawaki (~1940–1965). He later taught Joko Shibata.

Soen Shaku was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Kosen Imakita (~1878–1892) and at Keio University (~1882–1885). He served as chief abbot of Engaku-ji (1892) and held a post at Hanazono University.
Sogen Omori was a Buddhist studies and philosophy figure. He held positions at Kōho-in Temple (~1970–1994) and Hanazono University (~1978–1982), and he taught Tenshin Tanouye.

Sogyal Rinpoche was active in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Cambridge, as well as under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, and founded Rigpa (1975).

Soiku Shigematsu studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1961–1965) and under traditional teacher Kiju Shigematsu (attested 1981). Active in Buddhist studies, he taught American literature at Shizuoka University (~1975–2008) and held a post at Kansai Medical University.
Sojo Hirano was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and as shike at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992–1996). He also taught Sonja Arntzen.

Solomon George FitzHerbert is a Tibetologist who completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford. He has served as Departmental Lecturer in Tibetan and Himalayan studies at Oxford and as a researcher at the CNRS (attested 2019).

Somadeva Vasudeva is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He has held positions at the Institut Français de Pondichéry, Columbia University as Assistant Professor of Sanskrit, and Kyoto University as Professor (2011).

Somchai Kusalacitto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who received a Ph.D. from the University of Madras. He served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2003).

Somphong Santacitto works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a master's degree in Buddhist studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2006) under supervisor Phra Suthithammanuwat and committee member Watchara Ngamchitcharoen.

Sonam Chhoki is a Tibetology and history scholar who earned an M.A. from Jawaharlal Nehru University and a Ph.D. from SOAS University of London. She has served as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

Sonam Gyatso is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a research assistant at the Toyo Bunko and held a professorship at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014).

Sonam Kachru specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, earning a PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold. He held posts at the University of Chicago, Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, and Forum Transregionale Studien.

Sonam Thakchoe is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who completed a PhD at the University of Tasmania (~1998–2002) under Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas. He also held a post at the University of Tasmania (~2005).

Sonam Tsering is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Gray Tuttle, as well as teachers Khenzur Dawa, Drepung Khenzur Gyatso, Samdhong Rinpoche, Janet Gyatso, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Gyumé Khenzur Lobzang Trinlé.

Songeun Choe works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Choe studied under MA supervisor Myung-dae Moon and completed a PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).
Sonja Arntzen is a Japanology scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia (~1967–1979) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz. She also studied under Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.
